stories.headline: US indicts Sinaloa governor Rocha Moya and nine other officials on cartel ties; Sheinbaum demands evidence, defends sovereignty
stories.summary: The US Department of Justice unsealed an indictment charging Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya and nine other current and former state officials with conspiring with the Sinaloa cartel. Sheinbaum demanded 'irrefutable' evidence before acting, the SRE received extradition requests but declared them insufficiently supported, the FGR opened an investigation, and Rocha stepped back from his gubernatorial duties by requesting leave — losing his immunity in the process. The case triggered the largest political crisis of Sheinbaum's presidency, with opposition parties calling for a declaration of failed governance in Sinaloa and intelligence reports emerging that SEDENA and CNI had surveilled Rocha for years.

stories.headline: Mexico protests unauthorized CIA operation in Chihuahua after two US agents die in crash during anti-drug raid
stories.summary: Mexico issued a formal diplomatic note to the United States after discovering that US officials — identified in reports as CIA agents — participated in a narcotics operation in Chihuahua without authorization, with two of them dying in a car accident during the mission. Sheinbaum said Mexico was not informed until after the deaths, while Security Secretary García Harfuch met with Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos, who also denied prior knowledge of the unauthorized US presence.

stories.headline: CJNG crackdown intensifies: SEMAR arrests 'El Jardinero' as cartel loses succession leadership after El Mencho's death
stories.summary: Navy forces (SEMAR) arrested Audias Flores Silva, 'El Jardinero,' the CJNG's presumed successor to 'El Mencho' (killed in February 2026), after a 19-month intelligence operation culminating in Nayarit. Security Secretary García Harfuch declared the operation entirely Mexican-led. A federal judge subsequently suspended his extradition to the US, and reporting revealed SEDENA had received a tip about 'El Jardinero' as early as 2021.

stories.headline: Morena holds national congress, names Ariadna Montiel as new party president amid internal tensions over Sinaloa scandal
stories.summary: At its 8th Extraordinary National Congress, Morena unanimously elected former Social Welfare Secretary Ariadna Montiel as the new national party president, replacing Luisa María Alcalde who joined Sheinbaum's cabinet as legal counsel. The congress occurred against the backdrop of the Sinaloa indictment crisis, with party leadership calling for solidarity with Sheinbaum while pledging 'zero tolerance' for corruption among 2027 election candidates.

stories.headline: Morena's internal response to Sinaloa crisis: legislators defend Rocha's leave, others call for accountability
stories.summary: Within Morena, the Sinaloa indictment produced divided reactions: some legislators praised Rocha Moya's decision to take leave as a demonstration of legal cooperation, while at least one senator called for his full resignation, and the party officially declared 'no one is above the law.' The issue also generated visible damage to the party's public image, with a survey showing nearly half of Mexicans believe the accusations constitute a blow to Morena.

stories.headline: Trump mocks Sheinbaum at private dinner, imitates her voice over Gulf of Mexico naming dispute
stories.summary: At a private dinner of the Forum Club of the Palm Beaches in Florida, US President Donald Trump imitated Mexican President Sheinbaum's voice and recounted a phone call in which she asked him not to rename the Gulf of Mexico to 'Gulf of America,' adding that she 'probably doesn't like me so much anymore.' The comments drew extensive coverage in Mexican media and were widely contextualized alongside ongoing diplomatic tensions.

stories.headline: Banxico reports 410 billion peso operating loss for 2025, leaves government without transfer; May rate cut under consideration
stories.summary: Banco de México reported a net loss of 410,052 billion pesos for fiscal year 2025 — its second-largest on record — due to peso appreciation reducing the peso value of foreign-denominated reserves, meaning no remittances (remanentes) will be transferred to the federal government this year. Separately, Governor Victoria Rodríguez Ceja told Senate lawmakers the central bank is evaluating a final rate cut in its May 7 meeting to close out its current easing cycle, with the current reference rate at 6.75%.

stories.headline: Pemex reports 46 billion peso loss in Q1 2026 while debt falls to 12-year low; announces Petrobras cooperation deal
stories.summary: Petróleos Mexicanos reported a net loss of approximately 45,993 million pesos in the first quarter of 2026 due to lower export revenues and market volatility, though it reduced its total financial debt to $79 billion — the lowest since 2014. Separately, President Sheinbaum announced a planned trip to Brazil to formalize a cooperation agreement between Pemex and Petrobras covering oil exploration and biofuels, with a Petrobras technical team expected in Mexico in May.

stories.headline: Mexico's Q1 2026 GDP contracts 0.8%, worse than expected; analysts cut full-year forecasts
stories.summary: Official preliminary data showed Mexico's economy contracted 0.8% in the first quarter of 2026 from the previous quarter, surprising analysts who had expected weaker but positive growth. Several banks subsequently cut their full-year GDP forecasts, with analysts pointing to high uncertainty, energy sector headwinds, and weak public spending, though some noted the upcoming FIFA World Cup hosting could provide a modest boost.
